finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(), which only returns a boolean and never throws, and discards the result. The OWNER check is never enforced, so any caller can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (or any caller that reaches POST /tenants/{t}/wipe) with no OWNER role, and an attacker-chosen tenant path parameter.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant), which destroys all data for the tenant.

trace.note: Javadoc says requireRole returns a boolean and does not throw. The name suggests it enforces, which invites misuse.
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) and has no side effect.
The boolean result is discarded, so there is no branch and no exception.

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is the discarded requireRole call at line 26. The sibling export() correctly uses the throwing checkRole at line 32. No other filter, annotation or caller-side check exists in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: Only requireRole(u, "OWNER") at src/Admin.java:26, a boolean-returning, non-throwing function whose result is discarded. No other filter, annotation or caller check exists in the repo.
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls the non-throwing boolean requireRole (defined at 14-16) as a bare statement, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any user, unlike export() at line 32, which uses the throwing checkRole.

verdict_facts.guard_found: requireRole at src/Admin.java:14 (returns boolean, never throws); its result is discarded at line 26. The throwing checkRole (line 18) is used only in export(). No other guard exists.
verdict_facts.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls the boolean-returning requireRole as a bare statement, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any user without an OWNER role.

finding.claim: Authorization is not scoped to the tenant. The OWNER role is a global string in User.roles with no association to the tenant argument. Even once F1 is fixed, an OWNER of any tenant can wipe or export any other tenant (cross-tenant IDOR / broken object-level authorization). The same applies to export() at line 33.
finding.source: An authenticated user who holds OWNER for their own tenant. They supply an arbitrary victim tenant id in the {t} path parameter.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 and repo.export(tenant) at line 33, which destroy or exfiltrate another tenant's data.

trace.note: User has only name and a global Set<String> roles, with no tenant binding.
checkRole tests only role membership and never compares against the tenant.
export checks OWNER globally, then calls repo.export(tenant) with the attacker-supplied tenant at line 33.
wipe passes the attacker-supplied tenant straight to the repo.

finding.guards_checked: checkRole and requireRole check only the role string. No tenant-membership or ownership check is present in this file. The repo implementation is not in the codebase, so I could not confirm that it enforces tenancy. Severity depends on how the caller populates roles, for example per-tenant role strings, which are not evident here.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole (Admin.java:18-22) throws, but only tests the global role string "OWNER". requireRole (14-16) returns a bool that wipe() discards at line 26, so it is not a guard at all. Neither compares the user to the tenant. The repo interface (6-9) is not implemented in the codebase.
verdict.reason: Admin.java:32-33 checks only the literal global "OWNER" via checkRole (19) and then calls repo.export(tenant) with the path-supplied tenant. User (line 4) has no tenant binding, and the role is compared as the literal "OWNER", so it cannot be a per-tenant role string. Any OWNER can therefore reach another tenant's data, and wipe at line 27 has the same gap. The remaining caveat is that the caller and repo code are not visible.

verdict_facts.guard_found: checkRole (Admin.java:18-22, throws, used at line 32) and requireRole (line 14-16, result discarded at line 26). Both test only the global literal "OWNER" role, with no tenant comparison.
verdict_facts.reason: Admin.java:32 and :26 check only the global "OWNER" string (User.roles at line 4 has no tenant binding), then pass the caller-supplied tenant to repo.export/repo.wipe (lines 33/27), so any OWNER can target any tenant. The role string is the literal "OWNER", so per-tenant role strings cannot be in use, and the repo has no tenant-authorization parameter.
